title: Safety Benchmark Sensitivity to System Prompt Wording
original_idea: Evaluate three models on AILuminate using five systematically varied system prompts (varying strictness, persona, and topic framing). Compute variance in safety scores across system prompt variants and identify categories with highest sensitivity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The finding that safety benchmark scores are sensitive to prompt wording is already established by multiple papers. The specific AILuminate angle adds moderate but not groundbreaking value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very simple: write 5 system prompts, run AILuminate on 3 models with each, compute variance. Minimal technical skills required. Perfect for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3 models, 5 system prompts, 1 benchmark. Clear, tight scope with a single variable under study.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple papers address prompt sensitivity in safety evaluation: 'A Closer Look at System Prompt Robustness' (arxiv 2502.12197) directly studies system prompt robustness. SG-Bench (NeurIPS 2024) found that role-oriented prompts help defend against jailbreaks, few-shot demonstrations may induce harmful responses, and chain-of-thought harms safety on discrimination tasks. Research shows performance differences of up to 76 accuracy points from subtle prompt formatting changes. The specific study of AILuminate safety scores under 5 systematically varied system prompts (varying strictness, persona, topic framing) is not published, but the general phenomenon is well-documented.
